approvalTitle: Spec decomposition: 8 specs for matthewfield.ca rebuild
content:
# Spec Decomposition: matthewfield.ca

## Overview

Personal website rebuild for Matthew Field — replacing WordPress.com with a markdown-driven, Next.js static site. Eight specs ordered to deliver professional value early and defer complex features.

## Specs

### 1. site-foundation

**Scope**: Project scaffolding and core site shell. Next.js App Router, Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui, Velite content pipeline configuration, root layout, site layout with header/nav/footer, dark/light theme toggle (next-themes), landing page with hero cards linking to each major section, global styles and CSS theme variables, CSP headers in next.config.ts, custom 404 page, TypeScript strict mode, ESLint + Prettier config, .nvmrc + pnpm packageManager pin.

**Delivers**: A visitable site with a working landing page, navigation, theme toggle, and the complete development toolchain. Every subsequent spec builds on this foundation.

**End-to-end verification**: Visit the site locally, see the landing page with hero cards for each section, toggle dark/light mode, navigate between placeholder routes, confirm responsive layout on mobile viewport.

**Dependencies**: None.

**Design considerations**:
- Hero cards on the landing page will link to routes that don't have content yet — use styled placeholder pages or coming-soon states until their specs are implemented.
- Velite schemas should be stubbed for all content types (blog, projects, contributions, resources, pages) so later specs add content without reconfiguring the pipeline.
- Establish the card component pattern here since it's reused across blog index, project gallery, contributions, playground gallery, and the landing page itself.

---

### 2. professional-profile

**Scope**: Professional profile page (wide layout, MDX-driven visual resume/CV), contact section with LinkedIn/GitHub links, bot-protected email via react-obfuscate, contact form (name, email, message) with Resend API route, zod server-side validation, honeypot spam field. Standalone /contact slash page reusing the same contact components.

**Delivers**: The primary professional inbound funnel — employers and recruiters can view Matthew's experience and get in touch.

**End-to-end verification**: View the profile page with rendered MDX content, submit the contact form, verify email delivery via Resend, confirm email obfuscation works, visit /contact and confirm it uses the same contact components.

**Dependencies**: site-foundation.

**Design considerations**:
- Contact components (form, email display, social links) must be extractable to `src/components/shared/` for reuse on /contact.
- The Resend API route at `/api/contact/route.ts` needs zod schema validation and honeypot check.
- Wide layout — profile page uses more viewport width than standard content pages.

---

### 3. blog-core

**Scope**: Blog index page (reverse-chronological listing), individual blog post pages, MDX rendering with Shiki syntax highlighting and copy-to-clipboard button, tags and categories with filtering, estimated reading time, auto-generated table of contents from headings, previous/next post navigation, draft/unpublished status (excluded from production builds), footnotes/sidenotes via rehype/remark plugins, last-updated date display (shown only when updated after publication), code block styling.

**Delivers**: A fully functional blog where Matthew can publish markdown posts with rich formatting.

**End-to-end verification**: Create an MDX blog post with frontmatter, code blocks, footnotes, and headings. Verify it renders with syntax highlighting, TOC, reading time, prev/next links, and copy button on code blocks. Confirm drafts are excluded from production build.

**Dependencies**: site-foundation.

**Design considerations**:
- Velite blog schema: title, date, updated, description, tags, categories, series, seriesOrder, draft, body.
- Shiki theme selection — should support both light and dark themes matching the site toggle.
- Reading time computed via Velite schema transform using reading-time package.
- TOC generated from headings via rehype plugin.
- Blog content line length constrained to ~75 characters per product principles (readability), with generous whitespace.

---

### 4. blog-enhanced

**Scope**: Pagefind search integration (build-time indexing via crawler mode, client-side WASM search), RSS/Atom feed generation (static XML at build time), series/multi-part post grouping UI, related posts suggestions, social sharing buttons, reading progress bar.

**Delivers**: Blog discovery and engagement features — readers can search, subscribe via RSS, navigate series, and share posts.

**End-to-end verification**: Build the site, verify Pagefind index is generated, search for a known post and find it. Validate RSS feed with a feed validator. Navigate a multi-part series. Confirm related posts appear. Verify progress bar tracks scroll position.

**Dependencies**: blog-core.

**Design considerations**:
- Pagefind requires `next build && next start` + crawl in CI — this affects the build pipeline (package.json scripts, CI workflow).
- RSS route at `/feed.xml/route.ts` generates XML at build time. Blog posts only.
- Related posts algorithm — tag/category overlap scoring, simple is fine.
- Series UI — banner or sidebar showing all posts in the series with current position highlighted.

---

### 5. project-showcase

**Scope**: Project gallery page with visual preview cards, individual project subpages with full details (description, story, screenshots, GIF captures, technical details, links). MDX-driven content with image support.

**Delivers**: A showcase of Matthew's projects demonstrating active building.

**End-to-end verification**: Create an MDX project entry with images. See it in the gallery with a preview card. Click through to the detail page with full content rendered.

**Dependencies**: site-foundation.

**Design considerations**:
- Velite project schema: title, description, date, image (cover/preview), tags, links (demo, repo, etc.), body.
- Gallery cards need visual previews — images or screenshots as primary visual element.
- Content images colocated in `content/projects/`, copied to `public/static/` by Velite.
- Next.js Image component for optimization.

---

### 6. contributions-and-resources

**Scope**: Contributions gallery — single page displaying curated open-source contributions as cards (repo, contribution description, PR/commit links). Data from `content/contributions.yaml`. Resources/bookmarks page — entries grouped by category (title, URL, description). Data from `content/resources.yaml`. Both are single-page, data-driven, no subpages.

**Delivers**: Evidence of open-source activity and a curated reference directory.

**End-to-end verification**: Add entries to both YAML files. Contributions page renders cards with repo links. Resources page renders grouped entries with working external links.

**Dependencies**: site-foundation.

**Design considerations**:
- Both use YAML source data processed by Velite — not MDX (no prose body needed).
- Velite schemas for contributions (repo, description, prUrl, commitUrl, date) and resources (title, url, description, category).
- Contributions cards don't need subpages — all on one page.
- Resources grouped by category with a clean, scannable layout. "Blogs & Feeds" category serves as blogroll.

---

### 7. slash-pages

**Scope**: /about (personal page, MDX-driven), /colophon (tech stack documentation, MDX-driven), /now (current focus, MDX-driven), /sitemap (auto-generated HTML listing all pages), /slashes (index of all slash pages with descriptions).

**Delivers**: IndieWeb-convention pages that round out the site's personal presence.

**End-to-end verification**: Visit each slash page. /about, /colophon, /now render MDX content. /sitemap lists all site pages. /slashes lists all slash pages with descriptions and links.

**Dependencies**: site-foundation. Best implemented after other content specs are complete so /sitemap has full page coverage, but not strictly blocked.

**Design considerations**:
- /about, /colophon, /now use MDX content from `content/pages/`.
- /sitemap is component-only — queries all routes/content programmatically.
- /slashes is component-only — hardcoded list of slash pages with descriptions.
- /contact is already built in the professional-profile spec.

---

### 8. playground

**Scope**: Playground index/gallery page, playground manifest system (`playground/manifest.ts`), dynamic item loading via `[slug]/page.tsx`, playground layout with style reset (`all: initial`, `isolation: isolate`, `@layer playground`), CSS Modules for scoped styles, iframe isolation path with `/playground/[slug]/embed/page.tsx`, permissive playground CSP in next.config.ts. Include one sample item in each isolation mode to validate the architecture.

**Delivers**: A working sandbox system where self-contained mini-apps can be added independently.

**End-to-end verification**: Visit playground index, see gallery of items. Load a same-page item — confirm styles don't leak, site theme doesn't apply. Load an iframe-isolated item — confirm full isolation. Verify both work in production build (Turbopack/Webpack divergence check).

**Dependencies**: site-foundation.

**Design considerations**:
- Style isolation is the core architectural challenge — `all: initial` resets inherited properties, playground base stylesheet must re-establish `font-family`, `font-size`, `line-height`, `color`, `box-sizing`.
- Manifest pattern: single source of truth for `generateStaticParams`, gallery, and dynamic import.
- Verify in Vercel preview deploys, not just local dev (bundler divergence).
- Sample items should be minimal — just enough to prove both isolation modes work.

---

## Dependency Graph

```mermaid
graph TD
    S1[1. site-foundation] --> S2[2. professional-profile]
    S1 --> S3[3. blog-core]
    S1 --> S5[5. project-showcase]
    S1 --> S6[6. contributions-and-resources]
    S1 --> S7[7. slash-pages]
    S1 --> S8[8. playground]
    S3 --> S4[4. blog-enhanced]
```

Specs 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, and 8 can all proceed in parallel after spec 1. Spec 4 requires spec 3. The recommended linear order prioritizes business value (professional funnel first, then content, then polish).

## Cross-Spec Conventions

**MDX content pattern**: All prose content uses MDX files in `content/` with frontmatter metadata. Velite processes at build time into typed collections. Page components import from `#site/content`.

**Card component pattern**: A reusable card component established in spec 1 (for landing page hero cards) and extended/reused in blog index, project gallery, contributions page, and playground gallery. Cards share a consistent visual language but vary in content.

**Page layout pattern**: Server components by default. Content pages follow: import Velite data, render MDX body with custom components, wrap in page-level layout. Client components only for interactive elements (theme toggle, search, contact form, playground items).

**Velite schema pattern**: Each content type has a schema in `velite.config.ts`. Computed fields (slug, reading time) are Velite transforms. Content query helpers live in `src/lib/content.ts`.

**Contact component reuse**: Contact form, email obfuscation, and social links are shared components in `src/components/shared/`, used by both the professional profile page and /contact slash page.

## What Is NOT a Spec

| Item | Absorbed into | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Project scaffolding (Next.js init, pnpm, tsconfig) | site-foundation | No independent value |
| Velite pipeline setup | site-foundation | Infrastructure for all content specs |
| shadcn/ui installation + base components | site-foundation | UI foundation |
| ESLint, Prettier, Vitest, Playwright config | site-foundation | Dev tooling |
| CI/CD (GitHub Actions) | site-foundation | Delivery pipeline |
| CSP headers | site-foundation (base) + playground (permissive override) | Security configuration |
| XML sitemap (sitemap.ts) | site-foundation | Auto-generated by Next.js, simple setup |
| E2E tests for contact form | professional-profile | Test the feature where it's built |
| E2E tests for search, theme toggle | blog-enhanced (search), site-foundation (theme) | Test alongside feature |
| Link checker CI integration | blog-core or whichever spec sets up CI fully | CI enhancement |

## Open Questions

1. **Landing page hero cards before content exists**: Should hero cards link to styled "coming soon" placeholder pages, or should the landing page be iteratively updated as each section launches? Recommendation: use placeholder pages — they're trivial and the landing page should be complete from spec 1.

2. **Blog spec sizing**: The blog is split into core (spec 3) and enhanced (spec 4). Core delivers a fully readable blog; enhanced adds discovery and engagement. Is this split appropriate, or should they be one spec?

3. **Pagefind CI integration**: Pagefind requires running `next start` and crawling the local server during CI. This affects the build pipeline. Should this be set up in site-foundation (CI spec) or deferred to blog-enhanced (where it's actually used)? Recommendation: defer to blog-enhanced since it's the consumer.

4. **Sample playground items**: Spec 8 needs sample items to validate both isolation modes. Should these be real items Matthew wants to build, or minimal test fixtures? Recommendation: minimal test fixtures — real playground items are added ad-hoc after the system works.
